William Bedwell
wil'yam bed'wel
n. (William Bedwell, 1563–1632, English Arabist and translator of the Authorized Version)
Germanic Wilhelm, resolute protector, through William; English Bedwell, from a place-name.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

William Bedwell was the first Englishman to master Arabic, and he spent his life on it: a lexicon he never finished, an edition of the Arabic epistles of John, grammars, and the training of the next generation of orientalists. He was vicar of Tottenham, then a village north of London, and he sat in the First Westminster Company for the Authorized Version, where his Semitic learning bore directly on the Hebrew. Nobody in England had asked him to learn Arabic and nothing in his parish required it. He did it because the languages of the Near East throw light on the language of the Old Testament, and because a man who loves the text follows it wherever its vocabulary leads. The ready scribe is the Authorized Version's own word for such a man (Ezr 7:6).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines orientalist as one versed in the eastern languages, and lexicon as a dictionary.

expand to see more

O'RIENTALIST, n. An inhabitant of some eastern part of the world; one versed in the eastern languages and literature.

LEX'ICON, n. A dictionary; a vocabulary or book containing an alphabetical arrangement of the words in a language, with the definition of each.

SCRIBE, n. A writer; a notary; one who is skilled in the law; among the Jews, a doctor of the law.

GRAM'MAR, n. The art of speaking or writing a language with propriety or correctness.

Key Scripture

Ezr 7:6 — "This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the LORD his God upon him."

Ezr 7:10 — "For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments."

Dan 1:17 — "As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams."

Pro 9:9 — "Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning."

Modern Corruption

The first Englishman to master Arabic, vicar of a village that had no use for it.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The live misuse is the utilitarian question put to all such learning: what was it for? Bedwell's Arabic served the Hebrew, the Hebrew served the translation, and the translation served three centuries of English-speaking Christians who never heard his name. The chain is long and every link in it is invisible from the next.

The principle to recover is that God gives skill in learning as a gift and that preparation precedes usefulness by years. “he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel had given” (Ezr 7:6). The order of a scholar's making is stated twice over: “Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel” (Ezr 7:10). And the gift is named as a gift: “God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom” (Dan 1:17).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sopher (H5613), a scribe, a writer; Hebrew sakal (H7919), to be prudent, to have skill.

expand to see more

Hebrew sopher (H5613) — a scribe, a writer, a secretary; Ezra 7:6.

Hebrew mahir (H4106) — skilled, ready, quick in a work; Ezra 7:6.

Hebrew kuwn (H3559) — to prepare, to make ready, to fix firmly; Ezra 7:10.

Hebrew madda (H4093) — knowledge, science, learning; Daniel 1:17.

Hebrew lekach (H3948) — teaching, learning, that which is received; Proverbs 9:9.

Usage

"“he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses” (Ezr 7:6) — an Arabic lexicon he never finished."

"“God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom” (Dan 1:17) — nobody had asked him to learn it."

"“Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser” (Pro 9:9) — and he trained the next generation."
